newsitem.title: CHINA: China dissidents' jailing dismays world - Thatcher.
newsitem.headline: China dissidents' jailing dismays world - Thatcher.

text.p: Former British prime minister Margaret Thatcher said on Thursday that harsh sentences imposed on Chinese dissidents Wei Jingsheng and Wang Dan had caused dismay in the international community.
"The recent harsh sentences imposed on Mr Wei and Mr Wang has caused dismay in the wider world," Thatcher told a business summit in Beijing.
Wei, widely known as the father of China's modern democracy movement, was sentenced to 14 years in prison in December 1995 for plotting to overthrow the government.
Wang, former student leader of 1989 demonstrations for democracy that were brutally crushed by the army, is appealing an 11-year jail term on similar charges.

The jailing of Wang last month was the latest in a series of crushing blows to China's struggling pro-democracy movement. Most dissidents have already been forced into exile or are serving long sentences in prison or labour camps.
Wang had already served four years in prison for his role as a leader of the 1989 student demonstrations for democracy that were crushed by the military with heavy loss of life.
